en: Oṃ, homage to the illustrious Pratyaṅgirā!

Then, preceded by the recitation of auspicious verses (*svastivācana*), one should perform the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*). Having proclaimed the place and time: "I, [name], of [gotra] lineage, desiring the destruction of enemies and the pacification of all calamities and adversities, shall [recite] the Atharva-veda [mantra] encased within the *Śrīpratyaṅgirā-mālā-mantra*."
I shall cause the recitation of the nine verses [of the Amṛtanāda Upaniṣad] to be performed through a Brāhmaṇa of such-and-such a lineage named so-and-so.
Thus [is the rule] regarding Brāhmaṇas; for Śūdras and others, however, it is after omitting the nine verses of the Atharvaveda.
Now, the salutation to the Guru. Having performed three breath-controls (prāṇāyāmas), the rishi-assignment (ṛṣi-nyāsa) follows:
for this twenty-syllable Pratyaṅgirā, salutation to Bhairava, the Rishi; [place this] on the head. Salutation to Anuṣṭubh, the meter; [place this] in the mouth.

Salutation to the deity Śrī Pratyaṅgirā—[at] the heart. Salutation to the seed-syllable *hraṃ*—[at] the navel. Salutation to the power (*śakti*) *hrīṃ*—[at] the [forehead]. Salutation to the pin (*kīlaka*) *krīṃ*—[at] the feet. The application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of destroying my enemies during the recitation (*japa*). [Salutation] to all limbs. Now, the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*): *Oṃ krīṃ hraṃ* to the two thumbs.

Salutation. Oṃ krīṃ hraṃ, salutation to the two index fingers. Oṃ krīṃ hraṃ, salutation to the two middle fingers. Oṃ krīṃ hraṃ, salutation to the two ring fingers. Oṃ krīṃ hraṃ, salutation to the two little fingers.
Oṃ krīṃ hraṃ, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands.
In the same way, [the mantras for] the heart and so forth [are to be understood].

Then, having performed the worship of the water-vessel and the arghya-vessel with the six limbs, and having performed self-worship as well, one should draw the yantra upon a vessel made of gold or other materials. It is as follows: a square containing an eight-petalled lotus within a triangle.

Then, holding sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers, one should meditate: "I bow to the beloved Goddess Siṃhī, who has the face of a lion, whose blossoming eyes blaze, and whose busy front hands hold a trident, a large skull, a noose, and a *ḍamaru* drum; her cavernous mouth is formidable with its millions of fangs, and she possesses three blood-red eyes."

One should meditate upon the Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, who is like the moon, blazing, and adorned with pearls. Having thus meditated and worshipped her mentally, one should perform the consecration of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*). *Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ haṃ saḥ!
O life-force of the Goddess Śrī Pratyaṅgirā, abide here! Āṃ.*

Hrīṃṃ Kroṃ! O Goddess Śrī-Pratyaṅgirā, may all your senses—speech, mind, eyes, ears, and breath—come here and remain happily for a long time. Svāhā! Having thus performed the consecration of the vital breaths (prāṇapratiṣṭhā) and meditated once more, one should invoke her: Oṃ! O Goddess Pratyaṅgirā, come here; stay here!
Perform your empowerment here; be present here; accept my worship.
Having invoked [the deity] with the words, "O Lord, place my worship here;

accept it," one should veil [it] with *HRAṂ*, consecrate it as nectar with the *dhenu-mudrā* and *VAṂ*, perform the binding of the ten directions with the *astra-mantra* and the heart-mantra using finger-snaps, and [employ] the *āvāhanī*, *sthāpanī*, and *sannidhāyanī* [mudrās].
Display the mudrās: Sannirodhinī, Paramīkaraṇī, Sakalīkaraṇī, Yoni, Mahāyoni, Khaḍgabhūti, Nīlelihānā, and the others.

One should worship the Goddess with the ritual services (*upacāra*). Having uttered the root mantra: "Obeisance, I offer water for the feet (*pādya*) to the Goddess Śrī Pratyaṅgirā. In this same manner [one offers]: water for respectful reception (*argha*), water for sipping (*ācamanīya*), the bath (*snāna*), sandalwood paste (*candana*), vermilion (*sindūra*), unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), the sacred thread (*upavīta*), flowers (*puṣpa*), incense (*dhūpa*), lamp (*dīpa*), food offering (*naivedya*), fruit (*phala*), cooked food (*pakvānna*), and betel leaf (*tāmbūla*).
Having again offered water for sipping (ācamanīya) and the other articles, one should perform the worship of the protective enclosures (āvaraṇapūjā).
On the eight petals, starting from the east: Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Brāhmī. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Māheśvarī.

Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Kaumāryā. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Vaiṣṇavyā. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Vārāhyā. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Nārasiṃhyā. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Indrāṇyā. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍikā. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ.
Salutation to Cāmuṇḍā. Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to Vasundharā. Oṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to Mahālakṣmī.

Also for the faction of the enemy: Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ (2) obeisance to Stambhinī. Oṃ (6) obeisance to Kṣobhiṇī. Oṃ (6) obeisance to [Viṇyā]. Oṃ (6) obeisance to Bhramanī. Oṃ (6) obeisance to Bhrāmaṇī. Oṃ (6) obeisance to Raudrī. Oṃ (6) obeisance to Saṃhāriṇī.
Oṃ (6) homage to Mohinī.
Thus, having performed the worship.

Holding sandalwood, unbroken rice grains, and flowers, and reciting the root mantra, one should offer five handfuls in the *añjali* gesture while saying, "I worship the sandals of the goddess Śrī Pratyaṅgirā," and then perform worship with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*).

Having prepared an offering of black gram (*māṣa-bali*), sprinkle it with water while reciting *phaṭ*, veil it with *huṃ*, and render it nectarine (*amṛtīkṛta*) by means of the *dhenu-mudrā* while reciting *vaṃ*. Then, consecrate it three times with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*). Having uttered the root mantra, offer it with the *tatva-mudrā* while saying: "This offering (*bali*) is for the venerable goddess Pratyaṅgirā; *namaḥ*. Finally, present incense, lamps, and other offerings.

Now, having performed the recitation (*japa*) for one who is unable [to do so], and having offered it, one should prepare an offering of food (*bali*) for the protectors, sprinkle it with the *phaṭ* mantra, cover it, consecrate it with the *amṛtīkaraṇa* mudrā, recite the root mantra, and perform the *ṭhāka* rite. This is the root mantra: *KṢAṂ BHAKṢA JVĀLĀJIHVE KARĀLA*.
The mantra for the twenty enemies is: *daṃṣṭre pratyaṅgire kṣaṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ*.

Having performed the recitation (*japa*) sixty-four thousand times, and having completed the preliminary rite (*puraścaraṇa*) consisting of a fire-oblation (*homa*) of one-tenth that number, a libation (*tarpaṇa*) of one-tenth that number, and a feeding of Brahmins (*brāhmaṇabhojana*) of one-tenth that number, this mantra becomes effective. Hereafter follows the procedure for its application (*prayogavidhi*).

Now, the garland mantra (*mālā-mantra*): Oṃ hrīṃ! Homage to the one clothed in black! O you who possess a hundred thousand [forms], seated upon the lion throne, with a thousand faces, eighteen arms, great strength, and the prowess of great strength; O unconquered one, O invincible one, O Pratyaṅgirā, destroyer of the rituals of others, eradicator of the mantras of enemies!
O destroyer of supreme mantras, subduer of all beings! Keṃ Sauṃ Preṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ!
Protect me from all calamities and all misfortunes! (2) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Kṣīṃ Kroṃ! Paralyze the mouths of all the gods! (2) Cut through obstacles! (2) Devour all the wicked! Vaktrāla...

O tongue with lolling fangs, O terrible-faced one, shatter all mechanical devices! Tear asunder the chains! Put to flight the ocean-like hosts of the opposing asuras! O Mahāpratyaṅgirā, great Vidyā, embodiment of Rudra, bring about peace! Devour my enemies! Oṃ hrāṃ!
Hrīṃ hūṃ jṛmbhaya mohe (2) stambhe (2) oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ pratyaṅgire svāhā.
This is the garland mantra (mālā-mantra).

Now, the hymn to Pratyaṅgirā: *Oṃ, obeisance to the Goddess Śrī Pratyaṅgirā*. *Oṃ*, for this mantra of the hymn to Pratyaṅgirā, Mahādeva is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (*chandas*), Pratyaṅgirā is the deity (*devatā*), *Hūṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *Svāhā* is the power (*śakti*), *Krīṃ* is the pinning-stake (*kīlaka*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is in recitation for the sake of attaining my desired success.
The venerable Kubjikā said:
To the Blessed One, Maheśvara, who was seated comfortably and dwelling in tranquility.
Having approached, Pārvatī inquires after his feet.
The illustrious Bhairavī said:
The Dhāriṇī is the supreme vidyā, the Pratyaṅgirā, the most excellent among the intoxicated [mantras].
For the benefit of men and women, and for the sake of children and the momentary.
O Maheśvara, [you know] the five types of kings, from the Māṇḍalika down to the poor.
And for the learned twice-born, it is the special means that accomplishes all goals.
In all great fears, and in fears of lightning and fire.
In the destruction of tigers, elephants, rivers, streams, and oceans.
In all cases of malevolent magic, as well as in battles and fears of kings.
The goddess who generates good fortune and brings men under her control.
The Goddess, who bestows all accomplishments, has been recited and caused to be recited.
The great vidyā Pratyaṅgirā, proclaimed by Śiva, resides within his limbs.
For the sake of accomplishment, this supreme vidyā is always and eternally remembered.
It was spoken by the illustrious one of terrible form, and it is of a terrible nature.
Pratyaṅgirā is always proclaimed to be the counter-act to pratihati; of this there is no doubt.
With yellow sandalwood mixed with gorocanā and saffron.
And having written it on birch bark, it should always be worn by kings.
O best of gods, O Lord, tell me that vidyā.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Excellent, excellent, O highly fortunate one, you who act for the benefit of all living beings!
O Goddess, mother of good fortune, O slayer of the enemies of the gods, I shall speak according to your word; of this there is no doubt.
Pratyaṅgirā is the great vidyā that destroys all suffering.
She is the crusher of all the wicked and the liberator from all sins.
And she is the benefactress of all living beings, beginning with women and children.
The goddess who generates good fortune, as well as one who bestows strength and nourishment.
At crossroads, in houses, in forests, and in groves.
In a cremation ground, in an inaccessible place, in a terrible battle, or in the peril of enemies;
And at the king's gate, when famine and great terror have arisen.

Recited and taught, O Goddess, this Kāmadeva mantra bestows all accomplishments: ĀṂ ŚROṂ HSKHPHREṂ HSAUḤ KRĪṂ KRAUṂ JUṂ VLŪṂ KLĪṂ GLUṂ VLĪṂ KHROṂ KLŪṂ KLŪṂ KLŪṂ HRĪṂ NAVADURGĀ. OṂ AIṂ ŚRĪṂ HRĪṂ VRUṂ KRAUṂ. Śivāstra: OṂ NAMO.

To the Blessed One: *hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hreṃ hrauṃ hraṃ oṃ namaḥ śivāya astrāya phaṭ* || *Piṅgalāstra*: *oṃ kṣīṃ rūpāya piṅgalāstrāya phaṭ* || *Hskṣmlvryūṃ cintāmaṇi phaṭ* || *Āṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ āṃ pāśājuṣṭākṣara* ||
